messages:
eva: VectorAI just filed a case — huge spike of 503s on hosted /v1/generate for their tenant. p95 latency jumped and 5xx rate ~14% in the last 7m. Customers hitting streaming endpoints are timing out.

casey: checking logs now. I see repeated upstream worker exits from pool gpu-queue-7 around the same window. Typical pattern: runtime crash -> container restart -> 503s. Example log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z runner[12456]: runtime: signal SIGSEGV (11)
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z runner[12456]: panic: segfault at 0x0
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z kernel: nvidia: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z docker[pid]: container 9f8a... exited with code 139
```

tarun: nvml reports a reset around the same timestamps. Also seeing cuda illegal address errors in the infer logs before the SIGSEGV. Could be a bad kernel / quantization codepath with the swapped model.

linh: customer traffic profile: large-context streaming with toolcall enabled + high batch concurrency. VectorAI was using model variant rdx-qa-v3a (recent hot-swap at 13:50 UTC).

casey: good catch. model swap started 13:48 and finished 13:51 — aligns. Repro hypothesis: hotmodel swap to v3a triggers an attn kernel path that corrupts device memory under high concurrent toolcall streaming, causing illegal address then segfault.

eva: CS asked for immediate mitigation so their production is blocked. What can we do quickly?

tarun: short-term mitigation options: 1) route VectorAI traffic to fallback model rdx-stable-v2 (CPU fallback if needed), 2) reduce per-worker concurrency and dynbatch size for that tenant, or 3) pin them to Dedicated capacity if they need sustained throughput. I can push a traffic rule to route to fallback now.

casey: while tarun does that, we should collect core dumps and GPU diagnostic logs. Commands to run on node (run as root):
```bash
sudo journalctl -u infer-runner -o short-precise --since "2026-03-18 13:45" > /tmp/runner_journal.log
sudo cp /var/log/nvidia/* /tmp/nvidia_logs/
sudo gdb --batch --ex "thread apply all bt full" -ex quit /opt/infer/bin/runner /var/crash/core.runner.12456 > /tmp/backtrace.txt || true
```

linh: I'm starting the routing change to fallback model and throttling concurrency for tenant id "vectorai-prod" via the routing service now. ETA ~2m.

ops-bot: routing-change: tenant=vectorai-prod route=rdx-stable-v2 initiated by linh at 2026-03-18T14:04:22Z.

casey: confirmed some workers stopped crashing after the route change; 503 rate dropped to ~3% in the next minute. Good immediate relief. We still need root cause.

tarun: capturing driver and kernel versions from affected hosts: nvidia-driver 535.112, kernel 6.1.12-rt. I'll also collect nvml logs and GPU machine dmesg.

eva: draft CS message for VectorAI: "We've routed your traffic to a stable model variant to stop the errors and are collecting diagnostics. ETA for a full root cause update: 90 minutes. We'll share backtrace and next steps." Approve?

linh: approve. Add that we can offer rate-limited Dedicated capacity trial if they'd like to avoid hot-model-swap impacts.

casey: next steps checklist: 1) gather core/backtrace + nvml logs (tarun), 2) reproduce on staging with rdx-qa-v3a under high-concurrency streaming + toolcall (casey + infra), 3) run memory-checker build of runtime with ASAN/UBSAN for the suspect kernel paths, 4) write rollback policy to prevent hotswap to non-verified quant profiles.

tarun: I'm on point for logs and will upload artifacts to the incident folder /incidents/1711122222/artifacts when ready.

eva: assigning incident to oncall SRE @casey to lead triage and CS updates. I'll post status to the customer. :thumbsup:

casey: taking it. I'll link repro steps and findings in this thread once I can reproduce locally.

ops-bot: incident-note: slack-thread linked to internal ticket INF-2026-481. Created at 2026-03-18T14:05:00Z.
